boundaries.evidence: Faint, continuous light longitudinal line (much weaker than the white lines; colour unreliable in the stretched shadow). It lines up with the right end of the opposing-direction stop bar (bar spans x~80-148 at y~1155 px), and the opposing lanes with their arrows (x~50 and x~110 near S4) lie to its left, so it is taken as the left limit of the target carriageway. Very weak at S2; at S5 it is lost in a lighter mottled patch and is placed from the stop-bar end.

A second faint continuous light streak, parallel to the centre-line candidate and about 45 crop units to its right, visible as a weak but consistent brightness ridge from S1 to S4. Could be a worn lane line or a wheel-track wear streak; at S5 it disappears into the lighter patch, value extrapolated.
Clear solid white line running the full crop height to the crosswalk; left line of a pair of parallel lines about 25-32 crop units apart.

Clear solid white line, right line of the parallel pair; the narrow strip between this pair (roughly 1.5-1.9 m judging by car and crosswalk size) could be a bicycle lane or buffer. A car sits just right of it at S1 but does not hide it.

Soft dark-to-light transition from the dark road surface to a lighter paved band (sidewalk) from S1 to S4; no crisp kerb line. Near the junction (below about y~1170 px) the lighter surface steps in to x~335, where the crosswalk bars also stop (last bar ends near x~328), suggesting a kerb extension; the S5 value follows that edge.

partial_strips: An unmarked darker strip about 40-50 crop units wide (roughly x~335-390) runs along the right kerb from the top of the crop down to about y~1170 px (between S4 and S5), where the lighter kerb-extension/sidewalk surface replaces it; no painted line separates it from the surface to its left, so it is contained inside the strip between the right line of the pair and the kerb at S1-S4.
Left of the centre-line candidate are opposing-direction lanes (lines at x~0-15 and x~60-80, a stop bar and arrows), excluded.
cannot_determine: Whether the faint line at x~127-150 is really the centre line; it is very weak in the shadow and its colour cannot be judged, the main support is that the opposing stop bar ends there.

Whether the faint streak at x~173-196 is a worn lane line or only wear on the road surface; if it is not a line, the strip from the centre line to x~238-268 is about 110 crop units (~6 m) wide with no other visible line.
The function of the narrow strip between the paired lines at x~238-298 (bicycle lane, buffer or painted median) cannot be read from the image.
The strip from x~264-298 to the kerb is about 100 crop units (~5.5-6 m) wide with no visible internal line at S1-S4; it may combine a travel lane and an unmarked parking/loading strip.

The kerb edge is a soft tonal edge, not a visible kerb line; position uncertain by about 5-8 crop units. The kerb-extension reading at S5 is inferred from the lighter surface and the end of the crosswalk.

Right of the kerb, large white elongated objects lie at an angle to the road (possibly large vehicles or rooftop features of a leaning building); they are outside the carriageway and do not affect the traced boundaries.
